claims.text: The as-cast NbTiZrHfTa alloy has a high degree of atomic-level disorder.
Annealing at 900°C for 24 hours followed by slow cooling will reduce atomic-level disorder in NbTiZrHfTa.
The specified annealing treatment will produce short-range chemical order.
Annealing reduces the random distribution of elements in the alloy.
Reducing the random distribution of elements increases lattice symmetry.
Greater local order and lattice symmetry enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Improved local order raises the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
A higher density of states at the Fermi level makes Cooper-pair formation more favorable.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling will raise the superconducting transition temperature.
The annealed sample will have a measurably higher superconducting transition temperature than the as-cast sample.
The annealed sample will display a well-defined superconducting gap.
The as-cast baseline has a lower or poorly defined superconducting transition temperature.
Secondary-phase formation can independently influence superconductivity and complicate interpretation of the annealing effect.

contradictions.description: The boundary treats failure to reduce disorder as a condition under which the predicted effect may not hold, whereas the falsification rule treats lack of confirmed disorder reduction as falsification. This leaves ambiguity over whether unsuccessful mediator induction is an excluded condition or a decisive negative result.
